title: Broken: a deploy to prod changed dev resources
objective_text: Use bundle variables, targets and overrides to promote one codebase across dev, test and prod.
scenario: The orders bundle deploys dev and prod to one workspace, kept apart by catalog. After databricks bundle deploy -t prod from main, there was still only one nightly_orders job: the dev job had been updated in place, with its [dev] prefix gone and its schedule running, and its runs overwrote tables in the dev catalog. Find out why and fix the bundle without changing anything else.

fault.summary: dev and prod share one deployment state, and prod has no catalog of its own.
fault.symptom: A prod deploy updated the dev job in place instead of creating a prod job, and that job wrote into the dev catalog.
fault.planted: workspace.root_path is /Workspace/Deployments/${bundle.name} with no ${bundle.target}, so both targets keep their state in the same folder; and targets.prod sets no catalog variable, so prod uses the default, dev.

rules.why: The deployment state lives under root_path. Without the target in the path, every target shares one state, so a prod deploy updates the resources the dev deploy recorded. The default root_path ends in ${bundle.target} for this reason.
Every deploy writes under the team's deployment folder, whose permissions the platform team manages.
The bundle docs say not to use a /Shared path as production's root_path: every workspace user can write there.

explanation: A bundle keeps its deployment state, the record of which resources it deployed and their IDs, in a state folder under workspace.root_path. The default root_path ends in ${bundle.target}, so each target has its own state. Here someone set root_path without the target, so on one workspace dev and prod read and wrote the same state: deploying prod found the dev job in it and updated that job with prod's settings, which removed the development-mode prefix and unpaused its schedule. Putting ${bundle.target} back in the path gives each target its own state. Separately, prod never set the catalog variable, so it took the default, dev; a variables mapping under the prod target fixes that. Nothing else was broken, so nothing else should change.
hints: Where does a bundle keep the record of what it deployed? Look at workspace.root_path: is it different for dev and prod?
The default root_path is /Workspace/Users/${workspace.current_user.userName}/.bundle/${bundle.name}/${bundle.target}. Keep the team folder, but add the part that makes it per target.
Which catalog does prod write to? A target without its own variables mapping uses the variable's default.
Don't touch the modes, the branch, run_as or the hosts: they weren't the cause.
